title: ARKIV expiry metadata, origin indexing, and marketplace fee settlement
status: focused source-level origin and fee settlement checks pass; capability not accepted
changes: Marketplace fee collection validates transaction identity, denomination, and finite non-negative fee values before querying the database.
Fee values are normalized to the marketplace_fee NUMERIC(18,8) scale and rejected when they exceed its supported range.
Zero-fee transactions settle as a no-op instead of remaining indefinitely in the pending payout queue.

Distribution validates positive finite amount, recipient, and denomination before reads; it locks the fee row, requires the recorded denomination, and uses exact decimal accounting without the previous 0.001 over-distribution allowance.
Partial payouts leave the fee pending and distributed_at unset; status and distributed_at change only when the accumulated payout exactly equals total_fee.

Credit batch creation now accepts origin transaction ID/source/contract, requires ID and source together, persists the references to credit_batch, and inserts the class/transaction/source identity into the existing unique origin_tx_index within the caller-owned transaction. The CLI exposes these inputs.

Data Stream create/update accepts an optional caller-supplied timezone-aware expires_at, normalizes it to UTC, and the tenant-scoped Gateway accepts the value and includes it in its fixed read projection. No retention period is inferred.

scope_limits: The tests use mocked connections and do not prove PostgreSQL lock behavior under concurrent sessions.
Automatic retention-policy application and expiry cleanup are not connected to these timestamps; they remain metadata only.
Only Data Stream post write/read paths currently expose caller-supplied expiry. Expiry fields on impact claims, attestations, report snapshots, carbon credits, and retirements remain unintegrated.
Mocks verify origin-index write parameters and error propagation, but no disposable PostgreSQL race/replay check proves duplicate-origin conflict rollback.
The gRPC CreateBatchRequest does not yet expose origin transaction fields, although the CLI and service function do.
Reference fixtures, external marketplace settlement, and MAN-CAP-062 owner acceptance remain open.
